studies.Population: American adults in the Prostate, Lung, Colorectal, and Ovarian (PLCO) Cancer Screening Trial
studies.Ethnicity Basis: NA: no field-specific ethnicity evidence was available
studies.Reference: Adherence to the EAT-Lancet diet reduces the risk of renal cancer: Results from a population-based prospective study.
studies.Authors: Wei Q, Yang M, Zhu Z, Xiang L, Wang Y, Peng L, Tang Y, Deng S, Gu H
studies.comparison_type: Highest vs lowest quartile of EAT-Lancet diet adherence
studies.exposure_measurement_supporting_text: investigating the association between ELD adherence and renal cancer risk

sample_size.excerpt: A population-based prospective study of 101,755 American adults from the Prostate, Lung, Colorectal, and Ovarian (PLCO) Cancer Screening Trial.

cases.excerpt: Over 899,337.5 person-years of follow-up, 446 cases of renal cancer were identified.

effect_size.excerpt: In the fully adjusted model, a significant inverse association was observed between higher ELD adherence and renal cancer risk (HR for highest vs. lowest quartile: 0.65; 95 % CI: 0.49-0.88; P for trend = 0.002).

confidence_interval.excerpt: lowest quartile: 0.65; 95 % CI: 0.49-0.88; P for trend = 0.002).

comparison.excerpt: HR for highest vs. lowest quartile: 0.65

design.excerpt: Cox proportional hazards models were utilized to estimate hazard ratios (HRs) and 95 % confidence intervals (CIs)
